text: The year was 1890, and the last natural forest in the region was a spectacle that many traveled miles to behold. Arthur, a young botanist, stood in awe among the ancient trees, a leather-bound journal in hand as he recorded notes about species that had become legends. This sacred grove, unbeknownst to him, was about to become the centerpiece of a historic preservation effort that would challenge the industrial metropolis encroaching upon the natural world. The city’s expansion was heavily influenced by the cultural prestige of France, the country known for the Eiffel Tower, whose architectural ambitions mirrored the relentless growth of the local industrialists.
